newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close higher after Caldera remarks.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close higher after Caldera remarks.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed higher in thin trading on Monday after President Rafael Caldera reaffirmed his commitment to economic reform, traders said.

The market's 19-share index edged up 0.10 percent to close at 5,962.92 points, on trading of almost 10 million shares worth 3 billion bolivars ($6.38 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
Trading volume was light because of the Columbus Day holiday in the U.S.
"The only reason the bolsa didn't rise more is because of the U.S. holiday," said Investico broker Jose Antonio Oliveros.
"Local conditions are good. Rumors of a possible cabinet shuffle have been quelled, and there's plenty of liquidity," he said.
In a press conference Sunday, Caldera stressed his government's commitment to the so-called Agenda Venezuela reforms and sought to quell market rumors of an imminent cabinet shuffle.
Among issues that were traded, 25 rose, eight fell and eight closed unchanged.
Brokers saw a more active session on Tuesday as U.S. investors returned to the market.
